scoreBasis.visual: Unobserved: no current screenshot was available. CSS and drawing commands cannot establish rendered visual quality.
scoreBasis.audio: Unobserved: no listening. Scheduled clicks, notes and latency calculations are implementation evidence only.
scoreBasis.creativity: Code-defined interaction design only: eleven place rhythms, a common anticipating bar, a two-bar musical demonstration, gradual cube forms and saved personal phrases make a coherent musical progression. This does not rate how inventive it feels in play.
scoreBasis.sensation: Unobserved: no hands-on play, human timing evidence, device haptics or listening.
scoreBasis.cohesion: Source-visible relationship among counted steps, the common Line, shared timing window, earned gold, stars and progression. The intentionally sequential eleven-place path, slow transitions, black space and small cube are respected. Result context and cumulative-versus-current scoring remain less explicit than the rhythm model.
scoreBasis.polish: Code-defined judgement and result clarity only: accurate threshold display and minute formatting, silent-play reward restrictions, dropped-touch marks and surface-safe scheduled feedback. This score does not certify browser layout, motion, performance or perceived timing. The result card still contains two concrete labeling weaknesses.

strengths.observation: The place's pattern drives both judgement and the common bar; counted steps anticipate the cursor, and the place demonstrates its pattern for two bars. This is a useful teach-by-demonstration structure without enlarging the cube or adding another guide.

Results floor the displayed percentage instead of rounding an unearned 75% threshold upward, compare it with the stated threshold, and floor elapsed seconds before formatting the clock. The supplied tests explicitly cover 74.6%, 75% and the minute boundary; they were read, not run.

Touch-down timing accounts for reported audio output delay, stale feedback is cancelled or suppressed on surface changes, and rejected rapid touches receive a faint mark. The design has considered why a player's input should remain legible even when it does not score; its perceptual effectiveness still needs observation.

findings.issue: The required result content does not identify the completed place: the title is only Completo, Maestro or Remezcla, followed by stars, generic objectives, time and sparks. The optional narrator is not a reliable place label.
findings.consequence: A delayed or revisited result has less context, especially when the continuation button names a different, next place.
findings.remedy: Include the completed place name in the existing heading, for example Lago · Completo, while retaining the brief mode label.

findings.issue: The large stars use all stars ever earned for the place, while the checkmarks and percentage immediately below describe only this round. Neither section labels its time scope. A replay below 75% can therefore show a gold second star directly above an unchecked Ritmo row. Newly earned stars differ only through a glow.
findings.consequence: The player has to infer why an apparently failed rhythm objective still shows an earned star, weakening the result card's explanation of judgement.
findings.remedy: Preserve previously earned stars and add brief scope labels such as Tus estrellas and Esta ronda; optionally identify newly earned stars in text rather than relying only on glow.
